name: Effects inside an FM operator chain: per-operator EQ/phase/delay/comb/drive/decimator/waveshaper/punch applied to the signal before it modulates or is heard, for delayed-modulator bells, noise-excited comb strings and punchy FM attacks
goal: Treat each FM operator slot as an optional in-chain processor rather than a master effect, so the processed waveform goes on to modulate the next operator or is heard. Recipes: (1) a peak-EQ or phase (all-pass-like, with feedback) stage on a saw operator, with its frequency moved by mod wheel or LFO, for oscillator-level phasing; (2) a short delay with feedback on the modulator, which gives bells an inner 'chamber' echo when its ratio rises and its time drops, with a short envelope; (3) a comb resonator fed by a very short noise-burst operator, making a physical-model string, copied into three pairs (detuned, an octave up) and finished with chorus, delay and reverb as a 'virtual guitar'; (4) drive, decimator (bit/sample-rate reduction for early 8-bit wavetable tone), waveshaper and 'punch' on a modulator for aggressive FM attacks. Delta vs our KS-pluck, tuned-delay-resonator and FM ratio skills: placing these processors inside the modulation path.

source.title: Opsix Effects Mode: The Secret to New Sounds
source.transcript_note: Hardware FM synth walkthrough; mapped to generic operator-in-chain processing. Like/subscribe outro dropped.

prerequisites: FM synth whose operators can be processors (or a Web Audio graph where a modulator passes through Biquad/Delay/WaveShaper nodes before connecting to the carrier's frequency AudioParam, implementation note)
Chorus, delay and reverb for finishing

outputs.name: fm_fx_patch
outputs.description: Bell with inner echo, comb-string 'virtual guitar', phased saw, lo-fi or punchy FM voice

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Effects in this mode act on the operator signal in the chain, not on the final audio output like a master reverb.
Changing the noise operator's ratio does nothing; tune the comb pairs via pitch/detune instead.
The transcript gives no numeric settings beyond 4-bit decimation; set amounts by ear.
Web Audio note: a modulator delay inside an FM path needs a DelayNode between the modulator and the carrier's frequency param; very short feedback delays need an AudioWorklet (implementation note).

steps.action: Single-operator EQ/phase: put a saw on an operator, switch it to an effect slot with peak EQ (centre frequency + gain) or a phase stage; raise the phase feedback, then map mod wheel or a slow LFO to the effect frequency and/or mix. Mix 0 = only the incoming operator; 100% = only this operator.
steps.expect: Oscillator-level phasing/EQ sweep, no master phaser used

steps.action: Delayed-modulator bell: plain FM pair. Set the modulator (operator 2) to a short delay effect and raise its feedback; you hear the delay inside the modulation. Raise the modulator ratio (more harmonics), then shorten the delay time, give it a short envelope and increase the carrier's release.
steps.expect: Bell tone with an echo 'inside the bell chamber'

steps.action: Comb string: carrier operator set to a comb (resonator) effect fed by operator 2. With a sine source it just sounds like overdrive. Switch the source to noise with a very short, clicky envelope, set the mix to only the effect, raise comb feedback for guitar-like tones, lengthen the source envelope for longer strings, and raise the carrier's release.
steps.expect: Physical-model plucked string from noise + comb

steps.action: Virtual guitar: copy the comb pair to two more operator pairs (three identical sets). Detune one pair via pitch, and set the third an octave higher with a bit of detune, then combine all three and add chorus, delay and reverb.

Drive and distortion on an operator: distortion pushes a sine toward square-like harmonics (mix it back in); 'drive' on a saw acts like an analog oscillator overdriving a VCA/filter, adding subtle warmth.
Decimator: reduce bit depth (e.g. 4-bit) and sample frequency on a saw to recreate early 8-bit digital/wavetable-era oscillators. Lower frequency = lower resolution.
Waveshaper on a sine or saw operator: choose shaping curves to make wavetable-like waveforms (e.g. a 'super square'), and stack it in the modulation chain as a base layer.
steps.expect: New static waveforms from simple sources

steps.action: Punch on the modulator: set operator 2 to the punch effect and raise it so the FM attack hits harder; useful for aggressive attacking sounds.

verification: Raising phase feedback makes the oscillator-level phasing clearly audible on an analyser/by ear.
The delayed-modulator bell shows an audible echo inside the tone that changes with delay time.
Noise burst → comb with high feedback yields a pitched string; a sine source does not.
Decimator at 4-bit shows visible stair-steps on a scope.
